Hi Alex - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

What we heard
- Goal: move ShopLytics search + recommendations to Redwood Dedicated to meet latency SLOs (<200ms p95) and predictable unit cost.
- Expected traffic profile: daily baseline ~3k requests/day, peak bursts up to ~6k reqs/hour during promos, average request token size ~350 tokens, reranker + final generation on ~30% of requests.
- Compliance: SOC2 required, prefer VPC/private control plane; procurement will need typical evidence (see attached SOC2 checklist).

Integration & architecture items you flagged
- SDK setup & auth: SDKs (python/node) + API key auth; you asked about mTLS for the private deployment.
- Routing/fallback: region preference (us-east) with automated fallback to another pool; how we surface routing config.
- Structured output / tool calling: you want to call internal knowledge connectors and have predictable structured JSON outputs for downstream systems.
- Embeddings/reranker: want to replace current dense retriever with Redwood embeddings + a lightweight reranker to reduce false positives.

Dedicated capacity / autoscaling concerns
- Autoscaling policy: need to support sustained baseline capacity + burst autoscaling (short-lived spikes).
- Throughput sizing: want recommended GPU pool sizing for 150-300 concurrent inferences (with batching) and target throughput of ~800-1,200 tokens/sec during peak.
- Concurrency limits & queueing: ability to set per-route concurrency, queue depth, and prioritized queues for critical queries.

Attachments sent
- redwood-dedicated-arch-diagram.pdf (high-level draft)
- mutual-action-plan-shoplytics.xlsx (action items & timeline)
- SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (baseline checklist for procurement)

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (60m) with your infra + ML engineers to walk the arch and sizing - aim for week of Nov 23.
2) Redwood will run a short traffic model and provide sizing recommendations and a sample autoscaling policy.
3) Share a short SDK auth guide and mTLS options for private deployments.

Are you available Tuesday 11/24 at 14:00 ET for the deep-dive? I'll include Aditya on the invite to cover the autoscaling/throughput details.

Best,

Marissa - quick engineering notes we can bring to the deep-dive. High level assumptions based on Alex's numbers: avg request ~350 tokens, peak burst ~7k requests/min short tail.

1) Throughput & pool sizing (back-of-envelope)
- If we target ~1,200 tokens/sec sustained across the pool, with mixed workloads (50% gen, 30% rerank, 20% embeddings), a pool of 4 x A100-class nodes with optimized batching should cover baseline+short bursts with headroom.
- Concurrency per GPU: assume 8-12 concurrent in-flight requests for generative workloads with long tails; for low-latency rerankers we can use smaller batch windows to keep p95 <200ms.

2) Autoscaling policy suggestion
- min_capacity: 2 nodes (always warm)
- target_utilization: 60% GPU utilization
- max_capacity: 8 nodes (for promo bursts)
- scale_up_policy: step up by 1-2 nodes if avg utilization > target for 30s; allow burst capacity for sudden spikes (enable short-lived burst mode up to +2 nodes)
- scale_down_cooldown: 3 minutes to avoid flapping

3) Queues & concurrency limits
- Per-route concurrency tokens: allow configuration per route (e.g., /search-critical = 200 concurrent, /batch-async = 50).
- Queue behavior: default is backpressure with graceful 429s when queue depth > configured max, optional prioritized queues that let critical queries preempt if enabled.

4) SDK & auth notes
- SDKs already support key-based auth and will support mTLS for Private deployments. We'll prepare a short auth guide with config snippets (python/node).

5) Embeddings & reranker cost estimate
- Rough token-cost: embeddings ~0.5-0.8 tokens per token processed (depends on model); reranker pass is typically cheaper than full generation - estimate an additional ~10-20ms per call for a lightweight reranker model. We'll provide more concrete numbers after we run a small benchmark with ShopLytics sample traffic.

I can prepare a one-page sizing doc and a sample autoscaling config to share in the meeting.

 - Aditya
